You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 430910b1b93292d3a724c91123bb15bd32df1b5b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Or Gerlitz <ogerlitz@mellanox.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2015 15:14:06 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] IB/mlx4: Convert slave port before building address-handle

When multiplexling a MAD sent from VF, we should convert the port used
by the guest to send the packet to the actual physical port which will be
used to transmit the packet, before building the relevant address-handle (AH).

This is needed under VPI for single ported VFs, since the code that builds
the AH (mlx4_ib_query_ah()) makes decisions based on the input port. If we
use the port number provided by the guest, it might have different protocol
vs. the one this packat has to go from, and hence the result could be wrong.

So far, the conversion was done after the AH was built and it worked for
single ported Eth VFs which were not enabled under VPI. When adding support
for single ported IB VFs and VPI, we hit that.

Fixes: 449fc48866f7 ('net/mlx4: Adapt code for N-Port VF')
Signed-off-by: Or Gerlitz <ogerlitz@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
---
 drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx4/mad.c | 11 +++++++----
 1 file changed, 7 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx4/mad.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx4/mad.c
index 9cd2b002d7ae..ad6a8818608d 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx4/mad.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx4/mad.c
@@ -1365,14 +1365,17 @@ static void mlx4_ib_multiplex_mad(struct mlx4_ib_demux_pv_ctx *ctx, struct ib_wc
 	 * stadard address handle by decoding the tunnelled mlx4_ah fields */
 	memcpy(&ah.av, &tunnel->hdr.av, sizeof (struct mlx4_av));
 	ah.ibah.device = ctx->ib_dev;
+
+	port = be32_to_cpu(ah.av.ib.port_pd) >> 24;
+	port = mlx4_slave_convert_port(dev->dev, slave, port);
+	if (port < 0)
+		return;
+	ah.av.ib.port_pd = cpu_to_be32(port << 24 | (be32_to_cpu(ah.av.ib.port_pd) & 0xffffff));
+
 	mlx4_ib_query_ah(&ah.ibah, &ah_attr);
 	if (ah_attr.ah_flags & IB_AH_GRH)
 		fill_in_real_sgid_index(dev, slave, ctx->port, &ah_attr);
 
-	port = mlx4_slave_convert_port(dev->dev, slave, ah_attr.port_num);
-	if (port < 0)
-		return;
-	ah_attr.port_num = port;
 	memcpy(ah_attr.dmac, tunnel->hdr.mac, 6);
 	ah_attr.vlan_id = be16_to_cpu(tunnel->hdr.vlan);
 	/* if slave have default vlan use it */
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the port number used by guest virtual functions (VFs) when building the address-handle (AH) for multiplexed Management Data Blocks (MADs). The port number provided by the guest was not converted to the physical port used for packet transmission prior to building the AH, leading to potential mismatches in protocol, which resulted in erroneous address handling when the system was operating under Virtual Protocol Interconnect (VPI) with single-ported InfiniBand VFs. This issue was exacerbated by existing logic that only worked for single-ported Ethernet VFs without VPI support, revealing the need for the conversion step to occur before creating the AH.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:

    <text1>

    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the port number used by guest virtual functions (VFs) when building the address-handle (AH) for multiplexed Management Data Blocks (MADs). The port number provided by the guest was not converted to the physical port used for packet transmission prior to building the AH, leading to potential mismatches in protocol, which resulted in erroneous address handling when the system was operating under Virtual Protocol Interconnect (VPI) with single-ported InfiniBand VFs. This issue was exacerbated by existing logic that only worked for single-ported Ethernet VFs without VPI support, revealing the need for the conversion step to occur before creating the AH.
